Log on to your device, if you don't know how to do that, get a soho router because a Cisco one will be too advanced for you. Once log in issue the following commands.

en <enter> conf t <enter> username <username> privilege 15 password <password> <enter>

Default IP on those should be 192.168.0.1 but it might've been moved - to find out the correct IP on windows, do Start -> Run -> "cmd" -> type in "ipconfig" (no quotes), hit enter, and whatever comes up on the "Default Gateway: " line should be the lan side of your dcp3825.

Then do http://(the gateway ip) in a browser to avoid any of the bs that makes it search google for that ip rather than actually access it, and you should get the login prompt for the router's web interface.

Hopefully you've got those credentials, from there just change the wpa key/ssid or whatever to kick off any unexpected users. Failing that, phone the ISP if they set the logins, try blank for the defaults, or reset the device (hold reset for 10 or 30 seconds) and set the bastard up from scratch (if you've got the time + details to go through all that; avoid if possible for convenience :)
